AGENDA
  GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

 5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Kassakhian provided his comments regarding the attack of Hamas on Israel
  and wished for peace. He stated that Armenian-Americans are feeling a lot of trauma and
  déjà vu from seeing the same images of violence that happened in Artsakh. Kassakhian
  stated that he prays for peace for the people of Israel and Palestine. Kassakhian attended
  the Lithuanian Days Festival at St. Casimir Church Los Angeles and Octoberfest in
  Montrose. He also attended the Armenian Bone Marrow Walkathon and encouraged the
  public to support the organization by signing up for their bone marrow registry. Kassakhian
  invited the public to watch a documentary called “Cup of Salvation,” at the Glendale
  Laemmle Theater. He asked staff to agendize a discussion to consider supporting US
  Congresswoman Judy Chu’s and US Senator Alex Padilla’s call to urge the Biden-Harris
  Administration to expand the boundary of California’s San Gabriel Mountains National
  Monument.

  Councilmember Asatryan announced that October is also “Domestic Violence Awareness”
  Month. For anyone that needs assistance on domestic violence, YWCA Glendale provides
  legal assistance, adult and children counseling, housing navigation support, trauma support,
  childcare, emergency shelter, crisis assistance, financial assistance, and food pantry
  services. The public can reach YWCA Glendale at (818)242-4155 and the crisis hotline at
  (888)999-7511. Asatryan had an opportunity to go on a police car ride-along and asked staff
  to provide a memo on how the city is integrating and coordinating services for the unhoused
  population. She congratulated the Montrose Chamber of Commerce for a successful
  Octoberfest and the Glendale Chamber of Commerce for hosting the Jewel City Gala.
  Asatryan joins Kassakhian in his statement about what is happening in Israel and Palestine.
  As a response and a correction to a comment made earlier by a member of the public, she
  stated that there is no more blockade in Artsakh, the Armenian population was forced to
  deportation. Asatryan asked to agendize for discussion a better structure for the city’s
  friendship and sister cities and to provide an update regarding the work that is being done.
  She also asked to agendize for discussion recycling requirements for new construction
  multi-family units. Asatryan asked for an updated report on the Organics Waste and
  Recycling Program, which was discussed during the Council in Your Neighborhood Meeting
  on October 3 at Sparr Heights.

  Councilmember Najarian announced that the LA Metro Board will increase the northbound
  and southbound trains that serve the Glendale station which will not only make traffic on
  freeways better but also improve the air quality. He stated that he authored a second motion
  to make those trains silent and not sound their horns from Atwater to Northwest Glendale.

  Councilmember Devine stated that every week we hear about the Armenian Genocide and
  express our sadness for that community. She added that it seems that another genocide is
  happening in Israel. Devine expressed that her heart and prayers are with her Jewish
  friends and community and she wishes that those who have been captured will be rescued
  and safe.

  Mayor Brotman provided his comments regarding what has been taking place in Israel and
  Gaza. He called the purposeful targeting of civilians as horrific acts of terrorism. He
  expressed his sympathy to all the families who have lost loved ones or have loved ones who
  are held captive. He also stated that he hopes that Israel doesn’t act out of vengeance and
  commit the same offenses as targeting civilians in Gaza but be as measured as possible.
  He also stated that City Hall will be lit up with white and blue lights of the Israeli flag in
  support. Mayor Brotman stated that Adams Hill held an arts festival but he was unable to
  attend. He was able to attend October Fest which was a packed event.
